title: S2: Dispatch provider="claude" executor rows through run_worker with the row's model
spec:
Why: goal T-1334. After S1 (T-1335), pick_executor can return a provider="claude" row, but executor.start (executor.py:487) sends every non-codex pick to _exhausted(), which runs a fallback tier (sonnet/opus by complexity), not the routed model. Plug and play means a Claude row runs as itself. What: 1. orchestrator/executor.py start(): when ex.provider == "claude": acct = pool.pick("execute"); None -> bus.update status held, hold_reason "no account with headroom", return {"status": "held"}. Otherwise bus.update(task, executor=ex.id, tier=ex.id), ex.roll_day(); ex.day_tasks += 1; pool.save(), then run spawn.run_worker(task_id, account_id=acct.id) in a background thread registered in _fallback_threads exactly like _exhausted() (executor.py:535-569) and set handed_off=True so the dispatch reservation passes to run_worker. Return {"status": "dispatched", "executor": ex.id, "provider": "claude"}. No fallback/review_rule fields. ex is None keeps calling _exhausted(). Any other unknown provider -> held, hold_reason "unknown executor provider

". 2. orchestrator/spawn.py run_worker: model (spawn.py:1538) = pool.executors[t["tier"]].model when t["tier"] names a provider="claude" row, else cfg["models"][t["tier"]] as today. Execute branch (spawn.py:1564): executor field = the row id for a row-routed task, legacy f"claude:{tier}" otherwise; the "Claude fallback executor (Codex is unavailable)" prompt line only for legacy fallback, row-routed gets a neutral "You are the routed executor" line. executed_by (spawn.py:1657) uses t["executor"]. 3. orchestrator/daemon.py _codex_available (daemon.py:454): a provider="claude" row counts as available only when pool.pick("execute") returns an account. 4. Fix rounds: executor.resume_plan already returns fresh for non-codex parents (executor.py:279); keep it and cover it with a test. 5. README.md "Executors and routing" (README.md:278): document provider="claude" rows (id, model = full model id, quota_group, roles, complexity band), that Claude headroom comes from [[claude_accounts]], and the plug-and-play recipe: add a row to add a model, enabled=false on every codex row to run without Codex. No .orchestrator/pool.toml edit (Planner adds the opus55 row after merge). No new dependencies.
acceptance: tests/test_executor.py::ClaudeRowDispatch::test_start_runs_claude_row_with_its_model: with only a provider=claude row eligible, executor.start calls spawn.run_worker with an account_id, sets executor and tier to the row id, and does not call _exhausted
tests/test_executor.py::ClaudeRowDispatch::test_claude_row_holds_without_headroom: every account cooling -> status held, hold_reason 'no account with headroom'

tests/test_spawn.py::ClaudeRowModel::test_run_worker_uses_row_model: a task whose tier is a provider=claude row id launches claude with --model equal to the row's model and records executor = row id; a legacy tier 'sonnet' still resolves through [models]
tests/test_executor.py::ClaudeRowDispatch::test_fix_round_for_claude_row_is_fresh: resume_plan on a parent executed by a claude row returns mode fresh

constraints.interface_contract: Uses S1: Pool.executor_identity(field), Pool.is_claude_executor(field). A claude-row task has executor == tier == row id; its bus claim stays 'claude:<account id>' (spawn.py:1603) so running_claude_workers and max_parallel_claude_workers keep counting it.
